title: The Algorithmic Gaze: An Audit and Ethnography of the LAION-Aesthetics Predictor Model

bias_targets.methodology: Computed the Pointwise Mutual Information (PMI) of gender-related regular expressions (e.g., women vs. men) in image captions from the LAION-Aesthetics Dataset to measure disproportionate inclusion or exclusion above a specific aesthetic score threshold.
Computed the Pointwise Mutual Information (PMI) of LGBTQ+-related regular expressions in image captions from the LAION-Aesthetics Dataset to measure disproportionate filtering and exclusion.

Evaluated the aesthetic predictor model on the Metropolitan Museum of Art (MET) and WikiArt datasets to compare predicted aesthetic scores across different cultural origins, artist nationalities, and historical art departments (e.g., Western and Japanese art vs. African, Native American, and Islamic art).
Calculated the Pointwise Mutual Information (PMI) of religion-related regular expressions (e.g., Hindu, Christian vs. Jewish, Muslim) in image captions from the LAION-Aesthetics Dataset.

Analyzed the median scores and percentages of highly rated images across different art genres (e.g., landscapes, portraits) and styles (e.g., realism vs. cubism/abstract) in the WikiArt dataset to identify a systemic preference for photorealism.
